note: Hand-curated. Every fact comes from the program's official page. 'next' is filled in only once the official page announces the dates. collectors/programs-check.mjs re-reads each 'check_url' daily (except entries with check.auto false, whose sites refuse automated readers) and sets 'check.seen' when the dates on that page change; a person then reviews the entry and copies 'check.seen' into 'check.reviewed'.

items.name: Science Academies' Summer Research Fellowship
items.organizer: Indian Academy of Sciences, INSA and NASI
items.summary: Two months of research with a scientist, for students and college teachers, run by India's three national science academies.
items.who: Students in set years of BSc, BS, BE/BTech, BPharm, MSc, ME/MTech and integrated or dual-degree programmes, with an average of at least 65% in core subjects from Class X onwards; and college or university teachers. PhD students cannot apply.
items.stipend: A monthly fellowship for living costs at the place of work, plus round-trip train fare.
items.format: In person, at the guide's institute in India
items.usual: Two months with the assigned guide, at any time in the calendar year, preferably in summer. Selection letters go out around March or April.
items.last_edition: SRFP 2026: applications closed on 31 January 2026. SRFP 2027 applications close on 30 November 2026.

items.name: JNCASR Summer Research Fellowship Programme
items.organizer: Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research, Bengaluru
items.summary: Two months of research training with scientists at JNCASR and other leading institutes, between April and July.
items.who: Undergraduate and postgraduate students in science, engineering, pharmacy, technology, medicine, agriculture or veterinary sciences, in the years each discipline lists, with at least 60% in previous semesters. Some disciplines also require Mathematics in Class X and XII.
items.format: In person, at JNCASR and partner institutes
items.usual: One round a year. The official page says applications for SRFP 2027 will open soon.
items.last_edition: SRFP 2026: applications closed on 31 January 2026, and the selected list is published.

items.name: NCRA-TIFR Visiting Students' Research Programme
items.organizer: National Centre for Radio Astrophysics (TIFR), Pune
items.summary: A summer research project in astronomy and astrophysics, from May to July. Strong students may be offered a PhD place at NCRA-TIFR.
items.who: Students entering the final year of a BSc, MSc or BTech/BE (Physics, Astronomy, Applied Mathematics or Electronics), and students in the third or fourth year of an integrated MSc in Physics or Mathematics.
items.stipend: A stipend is paid. The official page does not state the amount.
items.format: In person, Pune; hostel place subject to availability
items.usual: Applications open in mid-January, with a deadline around mid-February. Offers are made by mid-March, and the programme runs from May to July.

items.name: SURGE at IIT Kanpur
items.organizer: IIT Kanpur, Office of Outreach Activities
items.summary: Summer research projects with IIT Kanpur faculty, ending with a project report and a poster presentation.
items.who: Indian students from other institutions: BTech, BE, BArch or BS students in their third year (fifth or sixth semester), and BSc or BA students in their second year, with a CPI of at least 6.0 (60%). Separate categories cover IIT Kanpur students and students from Nepal and Bhutan.
items.stipend: Up to 60 participants with a CPI of 8.5 or more get ₹16,000 for the programme, and up to 60 more get up to ₹8,000. Some are funded by their mentor's project.
items.fees: ₹750 to apply and ₹4,000 in administrative charges if selected (non-IIT Kanpur students). Hostel and mess are paid separately.
items.usual: Registration opens in early February and closes later that month. Results come in late March, and the programme runs from mid-May to mid-July.
items.last_edition: SURGE 2026: registration ran from 2 to 22 February 2026, and the programme ran from 11 May to 11 July 2026.

items.name: Summer Research Internship Programme, IIT Gandhinagar
items.summary: At least eight weeks on an IIT Gandhinagar research project, with a faculty mentor.
items.who: First-, second- and third-year undergraduates and first-year postgraduates. Indian students studying abroad can also apply.
items.stipend: ₹2,000 a week for most interns, for at least 8 weeks. It can differ for interns funded by a faculty project.
items.fees: Hostel: ₹175 a day, paid by every summer intern.
items.usual: Results are announced by the end of March. Interns commit to at least 8 weeks in summer and submit a report at the end.
items.last_edition: SRIP 2026: results are published on the official site.

check.reason: The site refuses automated readers, so WILSY does not check it daily.

items.name: Mitacs Globalink Research Internship
items.summary: A 12-week research internship at a Canadian university, with travel and living costs covered.
items.who: For the 2027 cohort: Indian nationals in a full-time BE or BTech programme at an institution on Mitacs' India list (through AICTE), with a cumulative average of at least 70%. IIT students are not eligible for 2027.
items.stipend: Funding towards a round-trip flight to Canada, housing, food and incidentals, and enrolment fees, plus emergency health insurance.
items.usual: One cohort a year. Internships run for 12 weeks between May and October.
items.last_edition: Summer 2027: the call for student applications has closed.

items.name: ISRO internship and student project schemes
items.organizer: Department of Space, Indian Space Research Organisation
items.summary: Internships of up to 45 days, and longer academic projects, at ISRO centres. You apply to each centre separately.
items.who: Indian citizens studying science or technology at UG, PG or PhD level, or who finished within the last six months, with at least 60% or a CGPA of 6.32.
items.stipend: None. ISRO pays no stipend and does not provide accommodation, though a centre may offer guest-house or hostel space if available.
items.format: In person, at an ISRO centre
items.usual: Each ISRO centre takes applications on its own page. The official page links to them.
